- 2026-02-02: Security questionnaire submitted. Key asks: on-prem deployment package, KMS integration, audit log retention (7 years), SOC2 report.
- 2026-02-28: Call (FF id ff_2026-02-28_lgt_onboarding_call). Legal introduced procurement checklist. Primary headaches: insurance limits, indemnity caps, export controls.
- 2026-03-04: Deep dive w/ security (FF id ff_2026-03-04_security_review). They flagged clause that ties SLA credits to uptime only; want SLA to include latency SLOs (p50/p95) for dedicated pool + explicit rollback/fallback policy. Quote from security: "We cannot accept vague patch timelines — need 48h critical patch window for dedicated nodes."
- 2026-03-07: SE follow-up (Carlos) to size reserved GPUs. Proposal: 10x A100-class GPUs reserved (estimated steady throughput ~6k tokens/sec aggregate, p95 < 50ms with batching). Need final runbook for autoscale/burst and expected latency under heavy KV-cache miss.
- 2026-03-09: Procurement emailed redline list. Major asks: (1) reduce Redwood indemnity cap to $5M (customer wants ~$50M); (2) require annual external pen-test report; (3) require extended SLA credits for compliance add-ons.

Use-case summary / technical constraints (short):
- Workload: sub-50ms p95 generation for trading assistant + <10ms latency for reranking endpoints. High availability across NA regions.
- Throughput: steady 40 concurrent sessions, 2x burst at market open (~90 concurrent) for 10-15 minute windows.
- Must support VPC + customer KMS, and option to run private deployment in customer colo for high-sensitivity flows.
- Routing/fallback: prefer multi-tier fallback (dedicated -> dedicated lower-tier model -> private/offline) rather than cloud-hosted public model to avoid vendor data residency issues.

Procurement/security blockers (detailed):
- DPA/MSA redlines: customer legal wants broader data use prohibitions and higher indemnity; conflicts with Redwood standard MSA. Procurement requests a DPA addendum that explicitly disallows model training on customer-provided prompts — Redwood to confirm contractual language.
- Insurance: procurement requires cyber policy proof and endorsement; wants Redwood to carry specific limits and named-insured evidence. This is delaying signature (legal needs cert by 2026-03-20).
- Compliance add-ons impacting SLA: customer requests extended forensic-retention and longer uptime credits tied to compliance add-ons. This would change the economics of Dedicated pricing (adds storage/ops costs) — finance to propose adjusted pricing.
- Technical verification: security ops requires a 2-week on-prem validation test for private package (patch cadence, exploit mitigation, network segmentation verification). Timeline shifts procurement ~4-6 weeks.

Next steps (short):
- Maya to coordinate Redwood legal + finance call with LatGuard legal 2026-03-12 to triage indemnity / insurance buckets.
- Carlos to deliver GPU runbook and formal throughput/latency projection by 2026-03-14 (includes burst behavior and KV-cache miss worst-case).
- Security to upload required SOC2/ISO artifacts and outline audit_log retention options.
- Procurement needs final MSA + DPA redline response by 2026-03-20 or deal stalls.
